subject: Dual-Marketplace Renewal: GCP Private Offer + AWS Marketplace cutover plan
messages:
From: Elaine Chang <elaine.chang@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing + split PO question for upcoming private offer

Hi Mina,

We're starting renewal planning for our Redwood footprint and want to consolidate where possible. We have two lanes in play: a GCP Private Offer (current primary) and an existing AWS Marketplace PO that Acme prefers to keep for burst/spot capacity.

Quick questions:
- Can Redwood accept a split-commit structure (majority on GCP private offer; a defined tranche on AWS marketplace PO) for the same annual term?
- What paperwork do you need from us to route invoices to separate billing lanes?
- Timeline: Can you provide a target for a DocuSign-ready private offer by early April?

I've attached our usage forecast for Q3–Q4 to help sizing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Elaine
Elaine Chang
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
Elaine Chang | Acme Analytics
Attachment: acme_usage_forecast_Q3-Q4.csv (CSV, 26 KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chang <elaine.chang@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + split PO question for upcoming private offer

Hi Elaine — thanks for the forecast and the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a split-commit across GCP Private Offer + AWS Marketplace for the same annual term, but it requires a small set of coordinated paperwork and invoice-routing rules.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Mutual Action Plan (MAP): we'll draft a MAP that lists deliverables — Private Offer creation, AWS Marketplace listing/acceptance for the tranche, DocuSign timelines, and acceptance checklist.
2) Billing lanes: Acme will provide the PO details for the AWS lane; Redwood will map the AWS Marketplace PO number to an isolated invoice path. GCP Private Offer will be a separate invoice with its own sales order number.
3) Commit split & discounts: we'll model the commit as 70% GCP private offer / 30% AWS marketplace (flexed by usage). We can apply annualized discount tiers on the combined committed spend — need to confirm final numbers.
4) Acceptance & capacity ramp: include a 90-day capacity ramp schedule in the MAP so your ops team can plan consumption.

I've attached an initial MAP draft and looped in Karthik for billing/invoice mapping and Marissa for legal/marketplace flows. Next steps: Karthik will share how invoices are routed and what fields AWS needs for PO mapping; Marissa will outline the private offer packaging. Can you confirm procurement legal contacts (for DocuSign) and preferred signature date window?

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (DOCX, 42 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chang <elaine.chang@acme-analytics.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + split PO question for upcoming private offer

Elaine / Mina — adding billing detail so the MAP reflects routable invoice fields.

Billing notes:
- AWS Marketplace lane: we need the Acme PO number (as it appears in your AR system) and the exact legal entity name for tax. AWS requires the PO to be visible at listing acceptance; we will provide the Marketplace listing ID and map invoice delivery to the AWS billing account.
- GCP Private Offer lane: we'll issue a Redwood sales order (RO-XXXXX). That sales order will be tied to your GCP Private Offer acceptance; invoices will be routed to the billing contact on the private offer.
- Tranche invoicing: suggestion is quarterly tranches for the AWS lane (to simplify cashflow), with monthly invoices for GCP. If Acme prefers consolidated monthly invoices with internal re-allocation, we can support that but will need an AR reconciliation cadence (monthly).

SLA exception request: Acme mentioned a dedicated region for low-latency inference. If you require a regional SLA beyond our standard SLA, that will be documented as an SLA exception and priced into the private offer. Please confirm whether the regional SLO must be contractually backed.

Attachment: billing-lane-mapping.xlsx (XLSX, 18 KB)

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

> Mina: Proposed approach (high level)...

From: Elaine Chang <elaine.chang@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>, GCP Partner <partner@gcpmarketplace.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + split PO question for upcoming private offer

Thanks Karthik / Mina — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Acme prefers consolidated monthly statements (one PDF) for internal GL reasons but still needs the AWS PO number printed on the invoice for traceability. If Redwood can generate a consolidated invoice that includes the AWS PO field (and a separate line for AWS-billed consumption), that would be ideal.
- We confirm the dedicated-region SLA must be contractually backed (we will put a formal SLO in the RFP addendum). Please include estimated uplift in price for the SLA exception.
- For timeline: our legal team prefers DocuSign out by 2027-04-05 so we can complete internal signoffs before mid-April.

Attached: Acme_PO_template.pdf (PDF, 14 KB) — this contains the PO fields we need on the invoice.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a final quote (with the combined commit and SLA exception pricing) by Fri, 19 Mar?
2) Can we schedule a 30-minute handoff call with your marketplace ops and AWS listing specialist — Friday morning PT works for us.

Appreciate it,
Elaine

> Karthik: Billing notes...

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chang <elaine.chang@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>, GCP Partner <partner@gcpmarketplace.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + split PO question for upcoming private offer

Elaine — thanks, this is clear and actionable. Quick summary of agreed items and next steps so everyone's aligned: 

Agreed:
- Split-commit structure accepted: target split 70% GCP Private Offer / 30% AWS Marketplace tranche.
- Consolidated monthly statement: Redwood will produce a single PDF invoice; AWS PO number will appear in the line-level metadata. We'll include a reconciliation appendix for your AR team.
- Dedicated-region SLA: treated as a contract SLO (exception). We'll include an explicit SLO appendix with uplift pricing.

Deliverables / owners / timeline:
- 2027-03-19 (Karthik): Final quote including SLA exception uplift and combined-commit discount tiers.
- 2027-03-22 (Mina / Marissa): Draft Private Offer package (DocuSign-ready) + AWS listing checklist.
- 2027-03-24 (AWS Marketplace specialist): Listing acceptance window & any AWS-specific PO mapping requirements.
- 2027-04-05: Target DocuSign send date (Acme legal preferred).

Attachments: I'll upload the MAP v1 with the updated billing notes and the acceptance checklist to the Drive link and share the DocuSign envelope once Marissa confirms legal language.

Next step: I'll send a calendar invite for Friday 19 Mar 10:00 PT for a quick handoff with our ops and the AWS listing rep. If that doesn't work for you, propose another slot.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Mina Haddad
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.docx (updated), acceptance_checklist_v1.pdf (PDF, 9 KB)
